root.name: English Opening: Symmetrical, Hedgehog, Flexible Formation
root.moves: 1. Nf3 c5 2. c4 Nf6 3. Nc3 e6 4. g3 b6 5. Bg2 Bb7 6. O-O Be7 7. d4 cxd4 8. Qxd4 d6 9. Rd1 a6 10. b3 Nbd7

overview: The Hedgehog: Black keeps pawns on a6, b6, d6 and e6 and pieces behind them, accepting less space, and waits to break with ...b5 or ...d5. White has a Maroczy-type bind with c4 and e4 and a space advantage, and tries to restrain both breaks while avoiding overextension. Positions are slow, manoeuvring and rich in strategic detail.

white_ideas.idea: Hold the Maroczy bind with c4 and e4 and restrict ...b5 and ...d5
Use the space for a kingside attack or queenside pressure

black_ideas.idea: Keep the Hedgehog compact and wait
Prepare the ...d5 or ...b5 break with ...Qc7 and ...Rac8

typical_structures.structure: Hedgehog with Black pawns on a6, b6, d6, e6

character.notes: A resilient, hard-to-break structure with slow manoeuvring.

structure.notes: Tension in the centre, a breaks pending for Black.

approach.notes: Black can adopt the Hedgehog against many White set-ups.

level.notes: Plans are subtle and hard to get right.

sublines_that_differ.name: 11.e4 Qc7 or 11...O-O
sublines_that_differ.how: Only different ways to set up the Hedgehog, same character.

character.reason: A Hedgehog is built to be hard to break down, with few ways to lose quickly.

structure.reason: The centre stays in tension with breaks pending, neither locked nor open.

approach.reason: The Hedgehog is a set-up Black can play against several White move orders.

level.reason: The timing of the ...b5 and ...d5 breaks is hard to master.

plans.reason: Black sits in a Hedgehog while White holds a Maroczy-type bind.
